title: Bekhorot 56
description: Why a purchased animal is exempt from animal tithe and why purchased fetuses are not, the prostitute’s payment that enters the pen, Abaye on gentile and Jewish prostitutes, and the mishna on brothers and partners: when they owe the premium on the half-shekel, when they owe animal tithe, and how dividing an inheritance changes both.

🤰 Ten fetuses bought in the womb all enter the pen: “at the time of doing”
💭 Rabbi Elazar saw Rabbi Yoḥanan in a dream

a1.he: מָה בָּנֶיךָ — אֵין בְּלָקוּחַ וּבְמַתָּנָה, אַף צֹאנְךָ וּבְקָרְךָ — אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ וּבְמַתָּנָה.

a2.he: וְהַאי בִּבְכוֹר כְּתִיב! אָמַר קְרָא: ״כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה״, אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לִבְכוֹר, דְּלָא אִיתֵיהּ בַּעֲשִׂיָּיה, דִּבְרֶחֶם קָדוֹשׁ — תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.

a3.he: וְאֵימָא: תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְחַטָּאת וּלְאָשָׁם! דּוּמְיָא דְּבִנְךָ — מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא, אַף צֹאנְךָ וְשׁוֹרְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא.

a4.he: וְאֵימָא: תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְעוֹלָה וְלִשְׁלָמִים! דּוּמְיָא דְּבִנְךָ — מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא בְּנֶדֶר וּנְדָבָה, אַף צֹאנְךָ וְשׁוֹרְךָ כּוּ׳.

a5.he: וְאֵימָא: תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְעוֹלַת רְאִיָּיה! דּוּמְיָא דְּבִנְךָ — מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן, אַף שׁוֹרְךָ וְצֹאנְךָ שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן.

a6.he: אִי מָה בִּנְךָ אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ כְּלָל, אַף שׁוֹרְךָ וְצֹאנְךָ אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ כְּלָל, אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָקַח עֲשָׂרָה עוּבָּרִין בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן — כּוּלָּם נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר?

a7.he: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״תַּעֲשֶׂה״ — בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה מִיעֵט הַכָּתוּב.

a8.he: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָקַח עֲשָׂרָה עוּבָּרִים בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן — כּוּלָּן נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר. וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן: הַלּוֹקֵחַ אוֹ שֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה פָּטוּר מִן מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה!

a9.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲזַאי בְּחֶילְמָא, מִילְּתָא מְעַלְּיָא אָמֵינָא. אָמַר קְרָא ״תַּעֲשֶׂה״, בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה מִיעֵט הַכָּתוּב. אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַלָּקוּחַ חָל עַל מְחוּסַּר זְמַן!

a10.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זוֹ אֵינָהּ מִשְׁנָה, וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר מִשְׁנָה — רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה הִיא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: מְחוּסַּר זְמַן נִכְנָס לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר, וַהֲרֵי הוּא כִּבְכוֹר, מָה בְּכוֹר קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ וְקָרֵב לְאַחַר זְמַנּוֹ — אַף מְחוּסַּר זְמַן קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ וְקָרֵב לְאַחַר זְמַנּוֹ.

a11.he: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב: אֵיזֶהוּ אֶתְנַן שֶׁנִּכְנָס לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר? כֹּל שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ לָהּ וְחָזַר וּלְקָחוֹ הֵימֶנָּה. וְהָא אִיפְּסִיל לֵיהּ בְּלוֹקֵחַ!

a12.he: אִישְׁתְּמִיטְתֵּיהּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָקַח עֲשָׂרָה עוּבָּרִין בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן — כּוּלָּם נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר.

b2.he: וְלוֹקְמַהּ בְּזוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית, וְתִיעַשְּׂרֵהּ אִיהִי! קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּזוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית לָא הָוֵי אֶתְנַן.

b3.he: כִּדְאַבָּיֵי, דְּאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה — אֶתְנַנָּהּ אָסוּר, וְכֹהֵן הַבָּא עָלֶיהָ אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם ״לֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ״. זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית — אֶתְנַנָּהּ מוּתָּר, וְכֹהֵן הַבָּא עָלֶיהָ לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם ״לֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ״.

b4.he: זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה אֶתְנַנָּהּ אָסוּר — גָּמַר ״תּוֹעֵבָה״ ״תּוֹעֵבָה״ מֵעֲרָיוֹת.

b5.he: מָה עֲרָיוֹת, דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בְּהוּ קִדּוּשֵׁי — אַף זוֹנָה, בְּהָךְ דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִדּוּשֵׁי.

b6.he: וְכֹהֵן הַבָּא עָלֶיהָ אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם ״לֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ״, דְּלֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהַאי לָאו זַרְעֵיהּ הוּא.

b7.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאַחִין וְהַשּׁוּתָּפִין, שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן — פְּטוּרִין מִמַּעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, חַיָּיבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה — פְּטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן.

b8.he: קָנוּ מִתְּפִיסַת הַבַּיִת — חַיָּיבִין, וְאִם לָאו — פְּטוּרִין. חָלְקוּ, חָזְרוּ וְנִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ — חַיָּיבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן וּפְטוּרִין מִמַּעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.

b9.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ — וְלֹא שֶׁל שׁוּתָּפוּת. יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ קָנוּ בִּתְפִיסַת הַבַּיִת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״יִהְיֶה״.

b10.he: וְהַאי בִּבְכוֹר כְּתִיב! אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לִבְכוֹר, דְּהָא אִיתֵיהּ בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְכוֹרוֹת בְּקַרְכֶם וְצֹאנְכֶם״, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.

b11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה, וּפְעָמִים שֶׁפְּטוּרִין מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן וּפְטוּרִין מִמַּעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, וּפְעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וּפְטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן.

b12.he: חַיָּיבִין בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה — שֶׁחָלְקוּ בַּכְּסָפִים וְלֹא חָלְקוּ בַּבְּהֵמָה, פְּטוּרִין מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה — שֶׁחָלְקוּ בַּבְּהֵמָה וְלֹא חָלְקוּ בַּכְּסָפִים.

b13.he: חַיָּיבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן וּפְטוּרִין מִמַּעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה — שֶׁחָלְקוּ בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה.

b14.he: חַיָּיבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וּפְטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן — שֶׁלֹּא חָלְקוּ בְּזֶה וּבָזֶה.

b15.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! חָלְקוּ בַּבְּהֵמָה וְלֹא חָלְקוּ בַּכְּסָפִים אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: כֵּיוָן דְּחָלְקוּ בַּבְּהֵמָה, גַּלּוֹ דַּעְתַּיְיהוּ דִּלְמִיפְלַג קָיְימִי, וְלִיחַיְּיבוּ בְּקָלְבּוֹן — קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b16.he: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָלְקוּ גְּדָיִים כְּנֶגֶד תְּיָישִׁים וּתְיָישִׁים כְּנֶגֶד גְּדָיִים.

b17.he: אֲבָל חָלְקוּ גְּדָיִים כְּנֶגֶד גְּדָיִים וּתְיָישִׁים כְּנֶגֶד תְּיָישִׁים — אוֹמֵר זֶה חֶלְקוֹ הַמַּגִּיעוֹ מִשָּׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָךְ.

b18.he: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חָלְקוּ גְּדָיִים כְּנֶגֶד גְּדָיִים וּתְיָישִׁים כְּנֶגֶד תְּיָישִׁים — אֵין אוֹמְרִים זֶה הוּא חֶלְקוֹ הַמַּגִּיעוֹ מִשָּׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָךְ.

b19.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָלְקוּ תִּשְׁעָה כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה, וַעֲשָׂרָה כְּנֶגֶד תִּשְׁעָה.

b20.he: אֲבָל חָלְקוּ תִּשְׁעָה כְּנֶגֶד תִּשְׁעָה וַעֲשָׂרָה כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה — אוֹמֵר זֶה חֶלְקוֹ הַמַּגִּיעוֹ מִשָּׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָךְ.

b21.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חָלְקוּ תִּשְׁעָה כְּנֶגֶד תִּשְׁעָה, וַעֲשָׂרָה כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה, אֵין אוֹמֵר זֶה חֶלְקוֹ הַמַּגִּיעוֹ מִשָּׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְכָךְ.

messages.text: Continued from 55b: the mishna taught that one who purchases an animal, or receives one as a gift, is exempt from animal tithe. Rav Kahana derives this from the verse “The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me. So you shall do with your oxen, and with your sheep” (Exodus 22:28–29).

Just as the redemption of your firstborn son does not apply to a child who was purchased or received as a gift, i.e., the mitzva applies only to one’s own son, so too, the mitzva of separating tithe from your flock and your herd does not apply to animals that were purchased or received as a gift.

notes.he: דלא שייכא בהו לקיחה ומתנה אלא אצלו נולדו:
notes.en: Your sons are not by purchase: purchase and gift have no place with them; rather, they were born in his own home.

notes.dh: ומה בנך אינו בלקוח ומתנה כו'
notes.he: וא"ת אין דנין אפשר משאי אפשר כדאמר ר"ע במנחות פרק התודה (מנחות דף פב.) וי"ל דהתם הוא דבבנין אב יליף פסח דורות מפסח מצרים אבל הכא היקשא הוא ומודה ר"ע דאמרינן בפ' בנות כותים (נדה לז:) על כרחך הקישן הכתוב וא"ת והא בההיא דתודה נמי מסקינן טעמא דר"א מועבדת שיהא עבודות של חדש שוות ביה ומוכח התם דהיינו היקש ואפ"ה פליג עליה ר"ע ולא קבלה מיניה ואין לומר משום דלית ליה לר"ע ההיא היקשא דהא בפסחים בפרק מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צו.) מקשינן ליה אהדדי לכמה דברים מהכא פסח מצרים לפסח דורות וי"ל דכיון דצריכא היקישא לשאר דברים לא שייך למימר התם על כרחן הקישן הכתוב לענין אפשר משאי אפשר וא"ת לר' אחדבוי בר אמי דאמר בפרק בנות כותים (נדה דף לז:) ר"א היא דאמר דנין אפשר משאי אפשר ולית ליה שינויא דעל כרחין הקישם ומה יתרץ כאן וי"ל הא דנעמידנה נמי כר' אליעזר אי נמי איצטריכא ליה היקשא דנדה לשאר דברים ומשום הכי לא מוקי לה כר"ע ומיהו קשה מההיא דאין משלשין במכות (בסוף) (דף ה.) דילפי לה מכות ממיתה והיינו אפשר משאי אפשר וגזרה שוה דהתם צריכה לכמה דברים:
notes.en: In brief: [Just as your son is not by purchase or gift…] One may ask: one does not derive what is possible from what is impossible [a son can never be purchased, while an animal can], as Rabbi Akiva says in chapter HaToda (Menaḥot 82a). Tosafot answer: there the derivation of the Passover of later generations from the Passover of Egypt is a binyan av, but here it is a juxtaposition (hekkesh), and Rabbi Akiva concedes to that, as we say in chapter Benot Kutim (Nidda 37b): “the verse juxtaposed them against your will.” They object: in that same passage about the thanks offering, Rabbi Eliezer’s reason is “and you shall perform [this service],” that all the services of this month be equal to it, which is evidently a juxtaposition, and still Rabbi Akiva disagrees; nor can one say Rabbi Akiva rejects that juxtaposition, for in chapter Mi SheHaya Tamei (Pesaḥim 96a) the two Passovers are juxtaposed for several matters. They answer: since that juxtaposition is needed for other matters, one cannot say “against your will” with regard to deriving the possible from the impossible. They ask further: according to Rabbi Aḥadvoi bar Ami (Nidda 37b), who says the passage there follows Rabbi Eliezer, who does derive the possible from the impossible, and who lacks the answer “against your will,” how is our passage explained? Answer: ours too follows Rabbi Eliezer; or else the juxtaposition of nidda was needed for other matters, which is why he did not attribute it to Rabbi Akiva. Tosafot leave a difficulty from “one does not impose a third” in Makkot (5a), where lashes are derived from death, which is the possible from the impossible, through a verbal analogy needed there for several matters. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: But this verse, which juxtaposes the firstborn son to an animal, is written with regard to redemption of a firstborn, not with regard to animal tithe.
messages.quote: so too, the mitzva of separating tithe from your flock and your herd

notes.he: ואת ילפת מינה מעשר ועוד בכור קדוש בלקוח ומתנה שהרי משעה שנולד קדוש:
notes.en: And he objects: But this is written about a firstborn, and you derive animal tithe from it! Moreover, a firstborn is sanctified even when purchased or received as a gift, since it is sacred from the moment it is born.

messages.text: The verse states: “So you shall do with your oxen, and with your sheep: Seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.” If this is not needed for the matter of firstborn animals, which do not require any action to sanctify them as the animal is already consecrated when it leaves the womb, apply it to the matter of animal tithe, where an animal is sanctified only when the owner counts it as the tenth animal.

verse.he: כֵּן־תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשֹׁרְךָ לְצֹאנֶךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים יִהְיֶה עִם־אִמּוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי תִּתְּנוֹ־לִי׃
verse.en: You shall do the same with your cattle and your flocks: seven days their male first-born shall remain with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.

notes.he: כן תעשה לשורך והא ודאי לא מצית מוקמת בבכור דהא מרחם קדוש ולא בעי עשייה שיקדישנה האיש:
notes.en: The verse states “you shall do”: “So you shall do with your oxen.” This you certainly cannot apply to a firstborn, since it is sacred from the womb and needs no “doing” by which a man would consecrate it.

notes.dh: אמר קרא כן תעשה אם אינו ענין לבכור
notes.he: תימה דבריש עד כמה לעיל (בכורות דף כו:) דרשינן לענין בכור כדאמר אמר קרא כן תעשה הוסיף לך הכתוב עשייה אחרת בשורך וי"ל הא דדרשינן ליה בבכור משום דכתיב בבכור אבל מאחר דאפקיה רחמנא בלשון עשייה דרשינן ליה למעשר משום דבכור לא שייך קדושת עשייה (קדושה):
notes.en: The verse states “So you shall do”; if it is not needed for a firstborn: It is puzzling, for at the beginning of chapter Ad Kama above (26b) we expound it with regard to a firstborn, as it says: “The verse states ‘So you shall do’: the verse added for you another ‘doing’ with your ox.” One may answer: we expound it with regard to a firstborn because it is written about a firstborn; but since the Merciful One phrased it in the language of “doing,” we also expound it for tithe, since sanctity through “doing” does not apply to a firstborn.

notes.he: דאיתיה בעשיה שמכניסן לדיר וקורא לו שם מעשר וסוקרו בסיקרא:
notes.en: Apply it to animal tithe: which involves a “doing,” in that he brings them into the pen, calls it by the name of tithe, and marks it with red paint.

messages.text: But instead one can say to apply this phrase: “So you shall do,” to the matter of a sin offering and a guilt offering rather than animal tithe, i.e., one should derive that these offerings are sanctified only if they originally belonged to the individual who is attempting to sanctify them, not if they are purchased or received as a gift.

notes.he: דלא לייתינהו מלקוח ומתנה:
notes.en: For a sin offering and a guilt offering: that one may not bring them from a purchased animal or a gift.

notes.he: דאיתנהו בעשייה שמקדישן:
notes.en: Apply it to a sin offering and a guilt offering: which involve a “doing,” in that he consecrates them.

messages.text: One expounds the phrase as referring to animal tithe because that case is similar to the case of: Your son. Just as your son does not come to be redeemed to atone for a sin, so too, the phrase: Your sheep and your oxen, discussed in the verse, is referring to animal tithe, which does not come to the Temple to atone for a sin. Sin offerings and guilt offerings are brought only if one commits a sin.

notes.he: דמשתעי בבכור אדם מה בכור אינו בא על חטא כו':
notes.en: Similar to “your sons”: the verse speaks of a human firstborn; just as a firstborn does not come for a sin, and so on.

notes.he: הא לא מצי אמרת דומיא דבנך בעינן דאינו בא על חטא והני באין על חטא:
notes.en: This you cannot say, for we require [a case] similar to your son, which does not come for a sin, and these come for a sin.

messages.text: But instead one can say to apply this phrase to the matter of a burnt offering and a peace offering, which can be brought even if one has not sinned, like the animal tithe.

notes.he: דאיתנהו בעשיה ואינן באין על חטא:
notes.en: But say: apply it to a burnt offering and a peace offering, which involve a “doing” and do not come for a sin.

messages.text: One expounds the phrase as referring to animal tithe because that case is similar to the case of: Your son. Just as your son cannot come in the form of a vow or a gift, so too, the phrase: Your sheep and your oxen, discussed in the verse, is referring to animal tithe, which cannot be brought as a vow or as a gift. It is not referring to a burnt offering or a peace offering, both of which can be brought as a vow or as a gift.

notes.he: בכור אינו נדר ונדבה אלא חובה:
notes.en: A firstborn is not a vow or a gift offering, but an obligation.

notes.he: לא ס"ד דומיא דבנך בעינן שאינו בא בנדר ונדבה לאפוקי עולה ושלמים דבאין בנדר ונדבה:
notes.en: This should not enter your mind: we require [a case] similar to your son, which does not come as a vow or a gift, to exclude the burnt offering and peace offering, which do come as a vow or a gift.

messages.text: But one can say instead that one should apply this phrase to the matter of a burnt offering of appearance, which one brings when he ascends to Jerusalem on one of the three pilgrimage Festivals. This offering is not brought for a sin, nor as a vow or a gift, as it is obligatory.

notes.he: שהיא חובה ולא על חטא:
notes.en: But say: for the burnt offering of appearance, which is an obligation and not for a sin.

messages.text: One expounds the phrase as referring to animal tithe because that case is similar to the case of: Your son. Just as your son does not have a fixed time of year to be redeemed, but is redeemed after the thirtieth day from his birth, so too: Your oxen and your sheep, discussed in the verse, is referring to animal tithe, which does not have a fixed time to be brought. By contrast, the burnt offering of appearance is brought only on the three pilgrimage Festivals.

notes.he: בכור אין זמן קבוע לקדושתו אלא כשנולד קדוש:
notes.en: A firstborn has no fixed time for its sanctity; rather, when it is born it is sacred.

messages.text: If the halakha of the tithing of a purchased animal is derived from the juxtaposition to the mitzva of redemption of a firstborn son, then all the halakhot of one should apply to the other: Just as your firstborn son cannot be purchased at all, under any circumstances, so too, your oxen and your sheep should not be subject to animal tithe if they are purchased at all.

If so, why does Rabbi Asi say that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: If one purchased ten animal fetuses while they were still in their mothers’ wombs and the animals were born once he already owned them, they all enter the pen to be tithed? If the halakha is derived from a firstborn son, there should be no concept of tithe in the case of purchased animals.

The verse states: “So you shall do with your oxen, and with your sheep: Seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.” The verse excludes purchased animals from animal tithe only at the time of doing, i.e., from the time the animals are fit to be sacrificed in the Temple, not while they are still in their mothers’ wombs, as at that time they are as yet unfit to be sacrificed on the altar.
messages.quote: why does Rabbi Asi say that Rabbi Yoḥanan says

notes.he: בשעה שהן ראויין להתעשר מיעט הכתוב שלא יהו לוקחין ובמעי אמן לאו שעת עשייה היא:
notes.en: At the time of doing: at the time when they are fit to be tithed, the verse excluded purchased animals; and in their mothers’ womb is not the time of doing.

notes.he: אמר רבא הא לא קשיא ההיא דרב אסי דאמר קרא כן תעשה שלא יהא לקוח ואימתי מיעט הכתוב לקוח בשעת עשייה כלומר בזמן שראוי להקרבה יש בו איסור לקוח אבל כשהן עוברין דלית בהו עשייה דלא חזו להקרבה לית בהו איסור דלקוח:
notes.en: Rava said: That of Rabbi Asi [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads “Rav Asi”] is not difficult. For the verse states “so you shall do,” that it must not be purchased; and when did the verse exclude a purchased animal? At the time of doing, that is, when it is fit to be sacrificed the prohibition of a purchased animal applies to it. But while they are fetuses, which have no “doing” since they are not fit to be sacrificed, the prohibition of a purchased animal does not apply to them.

messages.text: § The matter itself, to cite the relevant discussion in full:
If one purchased ten animal fetuses while they were still in their mothers’ wombs and the animals were born once he already owned them, they all enter the pen to be tithed.

notes.dh: לקח עשרה עוברין במעי אמן כו'
notes.he: לאו דוקא דהוא הדין נולדו כיון דהוי מחוסר זמן אי נמי נקט במעי אמן ואפילו לרבי שמעון בן יהודה דאמר מחוסר זמן נכנס לדיר להתעשר:
notes.en: He purchased ten fetuses in their mothers’ womb: this is not precise, since the same applies if they had been born, as they are still lacking time [to be sacrificed]. Alternatively, he said “in their mothers’ womb” so that the ruling holds even according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, who says that an animal whose time has not yet arrived enters the pen to be tithed.

messages.text: But didn’t we learn in the mishna: One who purchases an animal or has an animal that was given to him as a gift is exempt from animal tithe? If so, why isn’t the owner of these fetuses also exempt from animal tithe?
messages.quote: they all enter the pen to be tithed

messages.text: I saw Rabbi Yoḥanan in a dream, which is a sign that I am saying a proper matter in explaining his opinion. The verse states: “So you shall do” (Exodus 22:29); the verse excludes purchased animals from animal tithe only at the time of doing, i.e., from the time the animals are fit to be sacrificed in the Temple.

notes.he: הלילה נראה לי ר"י בחלום והואיל ונראה לי יודע אני בי שאומר היום דבר טעם:
notes.en: I saw Rabbi Yoḥanan in a dream: last night Rabbi Yoḥanan appeared to me in a dream, and since he appeared to me, I know of myself that today I will say a well-reasoned matter.

messages.text: The exemption of a purchased animal applies even to an animal whose time has not yet arrived, i.e., before it is eight days old and fit to be sacrificed in the Temple.
messages.quote: the verse excludes purchased animals from animal tithe only at the time of doing

notes.he: שאם לקחו קודם שבעת ימים ללידתו שוב אינו נכנס לדיר להתעשר וכל שכן אם לקחו גדול. והא מחוסר זמן דלא שעת עשייה היא וחייל עליה דין לקוח:
notes.en: Purchase applies to an animal whose time has not yet arrived: if he bought it within seven days of its birth, it no longer enters the pen to be tithed, and all the more so if he bought it grown. Yet an animal whose time has not arrived is not at “the time of doing,” and still the law of a purchased animal applies to it.

notes.dh: איסור לקוח חל על מחוסר זמן
notes.he: שאם לקחו קודם ז' ימים קודם שנראה להקרבה אינו נכנס לדיר להתעשר לעולם אע"ג דלקחו שלא בשעת עשייה:
notes.en: The prohibition of a purchased animal applies to one whose time has not yet arrived: if he bought it within seven days, before it is fit to be sacrificed, it never enters the pen to be tithed, even though he bought it not at the time of doing.

messages.text: By the same token, the exemption should also apply to a fetus, despite the fact that it is not yet fit to be sacrificed.
@Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim This baraita is not a tannaitic source that can be relied upon, as it is not accurate.
messages.quote: a purchased animal applies even to an animal whose time has not yet arrived

messages.text: And if you say this baraita is a tannaitic source that can be relied upon, it is only in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon, who says that an animal whose time has not yet arrived also enters the pen to be tithed, and in this regard it is like a firstborn animal.

notes.dh: ואם תימצי לומר משנה ודאי ר' שמעון היא
notes.he: דלדידיה מחוסר זמן שעת עשייה הוא ומשום הכי לקוח חל עליו ומיהו במעי אמו מודה דאין לקוח חל עליו:
notes.en: And if you say it is a tannaitic source, it is certainly Rabbi Shimon’s: for in his view an animal whose time has not yet arrived is at the time of doing, and therefore purchase applies to it. But with an animal in its mother’s womb he concedes that purchase does not apply to it.

notes.he: ושעת עשייה קרינן ביה. הלכך יש בו איסור לקוח:
notes.en: One whose time has not yet arrived enters the pen to be tithed: and we call it the time of doing; therefore the prohibition of a purchased animal applies to it.

messages.text: Just as a firstborn animal is sanctified before its time arrives to be sacrificed, but is sacrificed after its time, i.e., after it is at least eight days old, so too, an animal whose time has not yet arrived enters the pen to be tithed, and if it comes out as the tenth animal, it is sanctified before its time for sacrifice has arrived but is sacrificed only after its time, i.e., after it is at least eight days old.

notes.he: אף מחוסר זמן קדוש לפני זמן במעשר וקרב לאחר זמן:
notes.en: So too, one whose time has not arrived is sanctified as tithe before its time and is sacrificed after its time.

messages.text: Which is the type of animal set aside as payment to a prostitute, about which the Sages said (see 57a) that it enters the pen to be tithed? Any animal that he gave to her as payment and subsequently purchased back from her.
messages.lead: A tanna taught a baraita in the presence of Rav:

notes.he: ואם יש לו תשעה והוא חייבין במעשר ואם יצא אחד מן הכשירין בעשירי הרי טוב ואם יצא האתנן בעשירי יאכל במומו לבעלים:
notes.en: And then bought it back from her: if he has nine others besides this one, they are obligated in tithe. If one of the fit animals comes out tenth, well and good; and if the prostitute’s payment comes out tenth, it is eaten by its owners once it has a blemish.

notes.he: דמרבי ליה מתניתין מהכל נכנסין כגון שנתנו לו וחזר ולקחו ממנה. ובזונה עובדת כוכבים קא מיירי דלא איתחייביה במעשר ודמי כי חזר ולקחו ממנה כלקחו שלא בשעת עשייה ולית ביה איסור לקוח. הלכך נכנס לדיר להתעשר. וכתב לישנא אחרינא כגון שנתן לה עובר פרתו וחזר ולקחו ממנה בעוד שהוא עובר דלא חל עליה איסור לקוח. ומיסתבר כלישנא אחרינא:
notes.en: Which is the prostitute’s payment that enters the pen to be tithed, which our mishna includes in “all enter”: for instance, where he gave it to her and then bought it back from her. [A note in the printed text: it appears from our master’s wording that he did not have the Gemara’s reading “But isn’t it disqualified as purchased? It escaped him…”; this requires examination.] It speaks of a gentile prostitute, who is not obligated in tithe, and when he bought it back from her it is as if he bought it not at the time of doing, so the prohibition of a purchased animal does not apply to it; therefore it enters the pen to be tithed. Another version is given: for instance, where he gave her the fetus of his cow and bought it back from her while it was still a fetus, so that the prohibition of a purchased animal does not apply to it. The other version is more reasonable.

messages.text: But doesn’t it become disqualified from the status of animal tithe as a purchased animal, as he purchased it back from the prostitute?
messages.quote: and subsequently purchased back from her

messages.text: This statement escaped that tanna: As Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: If one purchased ten animal fetuses while they were still in their mothers’ wombs they all enter the pen to be tithed. Accordingly, the baraita can be understood as referring to an animal that was given to a prostitute as payment and purchased back from her while it was still inside its mother’s womb.
messages.quote: But doesn’t it become disqualified as a purchased animal

notes.he: להאי מקשה הא דאמר רבי אסי כו' והכא נמי כגון שנתנו במעי אמו:
notes.en: It escaped him: this questioner missed what Rabbi Asi said, and so on. And here too it is a case where he gave it to her while it was in its mother’s womb.

messages.text: But if that is the meaning of the baraita, why is it necessary to purchase the animal back from the prostitute for it to be subject to animal tithe? Let her tithe it herself, as it is not prohibited as payment to a prostitute, since it was in the womb when he gave it to her.

notes.he: כיון דבמעי אמו נתנו לה לא מיפסיל משום נתן במתנה ויאכל במומו אם יצא האתנן בעשירי ול"ל חזר ולקחו:
notes.en: Let her tithe it: since he gave it to her in its mother’s womb, it is not disqualified as one given as a gift, and it would be eaten with its blemish if the prostitute’s payment came out tenth. Why would he need to buy it back?

notes.dh: ואמאי מוקמינן לה בחזר ולקחן ותיעשריה איהי
notes.he: הזונה עצמה ובמעשר לית ביה איסור אתנן כדאמר לקמן כי משחתם בהם מום בם כל שהמום פוסל בו דבר ערוה פוסל בו ומעשר לא פסיל ביה מום:
notes.en: And why do we set it in a case where he bought them back? Let her tithe it, the prostitute herself. And with tithe there is no prohibition of a prostitute’s payment, as we say below: “because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them”: wherever a blemish disqualifies, a sexual transgression disqualifies; and a blemish does not disqualify tithe.

messages.text: The baraita is referring to a gentile prostitute, to whom the mitzva of tithing animals does not apply.

notes.he: בזונה עובדת כוכבים עסקי' דלאו בת עשורי היא:
notes.en: We are dealing with a gentile prostitute, who is not subject to tithing.

messages.text: But let the baraita establish this case, of an animal set aside as payment to a prostitute that nevertheless enters the pen to be tithed, as a case involving a Jewish prostitute, and let it be referring to a case where she tithes it herself.
This baraita teaches us that an animal given as payment to a Jewish prostitute does not have the halakhic status of payment to a prostitute, and is not prohibited for sacrifice.

notes.he: הך ברייתא דהאי אתנן דלא בר עשורי דזונה כותית היא דמיקרי אתנן אבל אי הוה זונה ישראלית לא מיקרי אתנן ואפילו למזבח שרי:
notes.en: This teaches us: this baraita teaches that this payment, which was not subject to tithing because the prostitute was a gentile, is called a prostitute’s payment; but had she been a Jewish prostitute, it would not be called a prostitute’s payment, and it would be permitted even for the altar.

messages.text: This is in accordance with the opinion of Abaye,

An animal given to a gentile prostitute is considered to be payment to a prostitute, which is prohibited for sacrifice on the altar. And a priest who engages in intercourse with a gentile prostitute is not flogged due to the prohibition of: “A widow, or one divorced, or a profaned woman, or a prostitute, these shall he not take, but a virgin of his own people shall he take to wife. And he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.”

verse.he: אַלְמָנָה וּגְרוּשָׁה וַחֲלָלָה זֹנָה אֶת־אֵלֶּה לֹא יִקָּח כִּי אִם־בְּתוּלָה מֵעַמָּיו יִקַּח אִשָּׁה׃ וְלֹא־יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ בְּעַמָּיו כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה מְקַדְּשׁוֹ׃ {ס}
verse.en: A widow, or a divorced woman, or one who is degraded by prostitution—such he may not marry. Only a virgin of his own kin may he take to wife— that he may not profane his offspring among his kin, for I GOD have sanctified him.

messages.text: Conversely, an animal given to a Jewish prostitute is not considered payment to a prostitute and it is permitted to sacrifice it. But a priest who engages in intercourse with a Jewish prostitute is flogged due to the prohibition of: “And he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.”

notes.dh: זונה ישראלית אתננה מותר וכהן הבא עליה כו'
notes.he: וא"ת והא אמר רבא בפ' מרובה (ב"ק ע:) דאתנן אסרה תורה אפי' בא על אמו ובתמורה תניא [רבי] (ר"ל) אומר אין אתנן אלא הבא לו בעבירה אבל אתנן אשתו נדה כו' י"ל דלא מיירי כדקיימא ליה באיסור ערוה דדוקא מיירי בדתפסי בהדי קדושין כדמפרש טעמא דלכך אתננה מותר והא דכהן הבא עליה לוקה בגיורת ומשוחררת שהיא זונה או שנעשית זונה מאדם אחר שהיתה עליו באיסור כרת כיון שבא עליה עשאה זונה או כמ"ד פנוי הבא על הפנויה שלא לשם אישות עשאה זונה והא דמשמע דלא משתכח בזונה ישראלית דתיעשרה איהי הוה מצי לאשכוחי באיסור ערוה אלא אתא לאשמועינן דזונה ישראלית אתננה מותר [וא"ת] לרבא דאמר בפ' בתרא דתמורה (דף כט:) דאחת זונה כותית וא' זונה ישראלית אתננה אסור תיקשי ברייתא וי"ל דלא מתנייא בי ר' חייא ור' אושעיא אי נמי הוה מצי למימר דשפיר משכחת לה דתיעשרה איהי אלא אשמועינן לקוח במעי אמו כרבי יוחנן ומיהו חידוש זה נמי שמעינן בשתיעשרה איהי כשנותן לה במעי אמו ולא מיפטר משום לקוח ושניתן במתנה:
notes.en: In brief: [A Jewish prostitute: her payment is permitted, and a priest who has intercourse with her is flogged.] One may ask: Rava says in chapter Merubba (Bava Kamma 70b) that the Torah forbade a prostitute’s payment even where a man had intercourse with his own mother, and in Temura a baraita teaches that a prostitute’s payment is only what comes to him through a transgression, but not the payment to his wife who is a nidda. Tosafot answer that Abaye is not speaking of a woman forbidden to the man as a forbidden relation; he speaks specifically of a woman with whom betrothal takes effect, as he gives this as the reason her payment is permitted. And the priest is flogged where she is a convert or a freed maidservant, who counts as a zona; or where she became a zona through another man forbidden to her under karet; or according to the view that an unmarried man who has intercourse with an unmarried woman not for the sake of marriage makes her a zona. As for the implication that a case of a Jewish prostitute who tithes it herself cannot be found: it could be found with a forbidden relation, but the baraita comes to teach that a Jewish prostitute’s payment is permitted. They ask further: according to Rava in the last chapter of Temura (29b), who forbids the payment of both a gentile and a Jewish prostitute, the baraita is difficult. Answer: it was not taught in the school of Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Oshaya [and is not authoritative]. Alternatively, the case of her tithing it herself could be found, but the baraita teaches purchase in the womb, as Rabbi Yoḥanan holds; though this novelty too would be learned where she tithes it herself, when he gave it to her in its mother’s womb, and it is not exempt as purchased or given as a gift. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: An animal given to a gentile prostitute is considered payment to a prostitute, which is prohibited for sacrifice on the altar, as Abaye derives a verbal analogy from the word “abomination” stated with regard to payment to a prostitute: “You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute, or the price of a dog, into the House of the Lord your God for any vow, for both of these are an abomination to the Lord your God,”
messages.quote: a gentile prostitute is considered to be payment to a prostitute, which is prohibited

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: בעריות כתיב מכל התועבות האלה ובאתנן כתיב כי תועבת ה' וגו':
notes.en: Regarding forbidden relations it is written “any of these abominations,” and regarding a prostitute’s payment it is written “for it is an abomination to the Lord,” and so on.

messages.text: and the word “abomination” stated in the verses discussing those with whom relations are forbidden: “For whosoever shall do any of these abominations, the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people.”

verse.he: כִּי כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְנִכְרְתוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָעֹשֹׂת מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּם׃
verse.en: All who do any of those abhorrent things—such persons shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.he: כתיב הכא כי תועבת ה' אלהיך הוא וכתיב בעריות כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות האלה בהך זונה דלא תפסי בה קידושי דכתיב לא תתחתן בם אתננה אסור:
notes.en: “Abomination,” “abomination,” from forbidden relations: it is written here “for it is an abomination to the Lord your God,” and it is written regarding forbidden relations “for whoever shall do any of these abominations.” With that prostitute with whom betrothal does not take effect, as it is written “nor shall you intermarry with them,” her payment is forbidden.

messages.text: Just as the verses discussing those with whom relations are forbidden are referring specifically to those women upon whom betrothal does not take effect, so too, the prostitute referred to in the verse is one upon whom betrothal does not take effect, i.e., a gentile prostitute.

notes.dh: מה עריות לא תפסי בהו קדושי
notes.he: דחייבי כריתות נינהו והכל מודים שאין קדושין תופסין בחייבי כריתות דאין ממזר אלא מחייבי כריתות במסכת יבמות (דף מט.):
notes.en: Just as with forbidden relations betrothal does not take effect: for they are those liable to karet, and all agree that betrothal does not take effect with those liable to karet, since a mamzer comes only from those liable to karet, in tractate Yevamot (49a).

notes.dh: מה עריות דלא תפסי בהו קדושין כו'
notes.he: תימה כיון דילפינן מעריות ה"ל למעוטי זונה כותית דבעינן דומיא דעריות דלא תפסי בה קדושין לדידיה ותפסו לאחריני לאפוקי זונה כותית דלא תפסי בה לא לדידיה ולא לאחריני כדאמר פ' החולץ (יבמות מה.) למ"ד כותי ועבד הבא על בת ישראל הולד כשר משום דלא הוי דומיא דעריות מהאי טעמא ורבא גופיה דמחייב בזונה כותית בפ' בתרא דתמורה (דף כט:) קסבר בפ' החולץ (יבמות דף מה:) הולד כשר וי"ל דגבי זונה כותית כיון דלא תפסי בה קדושי כלל כ"ש דגורם עליה שם זנות אבל לענין ממזרות אין לולד להיות ממזר כיון דאינה ראויה לאדם אחר יותר מזה:
notes.en: Just as with forbidden relations, with whom betrothal does not take effect: It is puzzling: since we derive from forbidden relations, he should have excluded a gentile prostitute, for we require a case similar to forbidden relations, with whom betrothal does not take effect for him but does take effect for others. That excludes a gentile prostitute, with whom it takes effect neither for him nor for others, as is said in chapter HaḤoletz (Yevamot 45a) according to the view that when a gentile or a slave has intercourse with a Jewish woman the child is fit, for this very reason, that it is not similar to forbidden relations. And Rava himself, who forbids [the payment of] a gentile prostitute in the last chapter of Temura (29b), holds in chapter HaḤoletz (Yevamot 45b) that the child is fit. One may answer: with a gentile prostitute, since betrothal does not take effect with her at all, all the more so is she called a harlot; but with regard to mamzer status, the child is not a mamzer, since she is no more fit for another man than for this one.

messages.text: Abaye further stated: And a priest who engages in intercourse with her is not flogged due to the prohibition of: “And he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.” The reason is that the Merciful One states that he should not profane his seed, i.e., his children, and any children born from this gentile prostitute are not considered to be his seed, as the children of a gentile mother are gentiles.
messages.quote: And a priest who engages in intercourse with a gentile prostitute is not flogged

notes.he: דהולד הולך אחר הכותית בפ"ב דיבמות (דף כג.) בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך ואין (בן) בנך הבא מן הכותית קרוי בנך אלא בנה:
notes.en: Is not his seed: for the child follows the gentile mother, as in chapter 2 of Yevamot (23a): your son from a Jewish woman is called your son, but your son from a gentile woman is not called your son but her son.

notes.he: כדגמרינן ביבמות בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה וכדמפרש התם. והאי זרעיה הוא דתפסי בה קידושי:
notes.en: And this one is not his seed: as we learn in Yevamot, your son from a Jewish woman is called your son, but your son from a gentile woman is not called your son but her son, as explained there. But this one [the child of a Jewish woman] is his seed, since betrothal takes effect with her.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to brothers and partners, i.e., brothers who are partners in the inheritance of their father, when they are obligated to add the premium [bakalbon] to their annual half-shekel payment to the Temple they are exempt from animal tithe. Conversely, those whose halakhic status is like that of sons who are supported by their father and are obligated to separate animal tithe are exempt from adding the premium.

notes.dh: מתני' האחין שהן שותפין כשהן חייבין בקלבון
notes.he: כדמפרש לקמן שחלקו בנכסי אביהן ואח"כ נשתתפו ואם שוקלין הסלע שלם [דהיינו] שני חצאי שקליהם ביחד (יהו כולן) חייבין לתת כל אחד ואחד מעה קטנה לקלבון דהא שני ממונות הן והרי הן כשאר בני אדם שהשוקל שקלו נותן עמו קלבון דהוא קלבון להכרע וי"א לחילוף שאין שני חצאי סלע יוצאין בסלע בלא חילוף מועט והואיל ורוב בני אדם נותנין כל אחד מחצית הסלע וקלבונו עמו כי מצטרפי נמי שנים ויהבי סלע שלם יהבי נמי קלבון שני והני אחין שחלקו וחזרו ונשתתפו דהכא הן כשאר שותפין דעלמא וחייבין בקלבון שני:
notes.en: MISHNA. Brothers who are partners, when they are obligated in the premium: as explained below, where they divided their father’s property and afterward became partners. If they pay a whole sela, that is, their two half-shekels together, each of them must give a small ma’a as a premium, since they are two separate funds, and they are like other people, where one who pays his shekel gives a premium with it. It is a premium to make up the weight; and some say, for the exchange, since two half-sela coins are not changed for a sela without a small fee. Since most people each give half a sela with its premium, when two join and give a whole sela they also give a second premium. These brothers who divided and became partners again are like ordinary partners and are obligated in a second premium.

notes.he: כל ימי שותפותן לעולם כדקתני בברייתא בגמרא יהיה לך ולא של שותפות:
notes.en: Exempt from animal tithe: for all the days of their partnership, as taught in the baraita in the Gemara: “shall be yours,” and not that of a partnership.

notes.he: כגון שלא חלקו ועדיין תפיסת בית ירושת אביהן קיימת דלא הוו כשותפות כדאמר בגמרא יכול אפי' קנו בתפיסת הבית ת"ל יהיה אלמא כאביהן דמו:
notes.en: And when they are obligated in animal tithe: for instance, where they did not divide and the possession of their father’s inherited house still stands, which is not like a partnership, as said in the Gemara: “One might think even if they acquired from the possession of the house; the verse states ‘shall be.’” Evidently they are like their father.

notes.he: שני אם נותנין בין שניהם סלע שלם דבמקום אביהן קיימי נכסי ואילו הוה יהיב אבוהון סלע על ב' בניו לא היה נותן קלבון לחילוף שכן דרך לעולם שהמחוייב שני חצאי שקלים נותן שקל שלם ולא הוי כשני אנשים המצרפין שני חצאי סלעיהם לסלע שלם:
notes.en: Exempt from the premium: the second premium, if the two of them together give a whole sela, for the property stands in their father’s place. Had their father given a sela for his two sons, he would not have given a premium for the exchange, for that is always the way: one obligated in two half-shekels gives a whole shekel, and it is not like two people who combine their two half-sela coins into a whole sela.

notes.he: מיירי באחין שחלקו ירושתן:
notes.en: Brothers who are partners: it speaks of brothers who divided their inheritance.

messages.text: If the brothers acquired the animals through inheritance from the property in the possession of their father’s house they are obligated in animal tithe; but if not, they are exempt.

notes.he: במעשר בהמה כדאמרינן בגמ'. והאי קנו לא לקחו במעות אלא קנו שנפלה להם בהמה מאביהם:
notes.en: If they acquired from the possession of the house, they are obligated: in animal tithe, as we say in the Gemara. This “acquired” does not mean they bought with money, but that an animal fell to them from their father.

messages.text: How so? If they divided the inheritance between them and then reentered a partnership, they are obligated to add the premium and are exempt from animal tithe.

notes.he: הוו כשותפין דעלמא ופטורין ממעשר בהמה וחייבין בקלבון:
notes.en: They divided and became partners again: they are like ordinary partners, exempt from animal tithe and obligated in the premium.

notes.he: הואיל וחלקו אם נתנו ביחד שקל צריכין להוסיף קולבון דהיינו פונדיון. שכך מכריעין ב' חצאי שקל יותר משקל ואע"ג דחזרו ונשתתפו לא נפטרו מקולבון דכיון דחלקו הוי ליה כשני ממונות ופטור ממעשר בהמה משום דכיון דחלקו הרי הן כלקוחות ולקוח פטור ממעשר בהמה. ועוד כיון דנשתתפו נפטרו מן (הבכורה) [המעשר] כדאמרי' בגמ' קנו בתפוס' הבית כלומר שלא חלקו ירושתן ומעצמן השביחו וילדו חייבין במעשר בהמה דנתחייבו הנכסים במעשר כבתחלה בחיי אביהן. ואם לאו שחלקו ונשתתפו והדר ילדו פטור חלקו וחזרו ונשתתפו היינו פירוש דרישא:
notes.en: And became partners again, that they are obligated in the premium: since they divided, if they gave a shekel together they must add a premium, which is a pundeyon, for that is how two half-shekels are made to outweigh a shekel. Even though they became partners again they are not released from the premium, since once they divided it is two separate funds. And they are exempt from animal tithe because once they divided they are like purchasers, and a purchased animal is exempt from animal tithe. Moreover, since they became partners, they are exempt from the tithe [the printed text reads “firstborn,” corrected to “tithe”], as we say in the Gemara. “They acquired from the possession of the house”: that is, they did not divide their inheritance, and [the animals] grew and gave birth on their own; they are obligated in animal tithe, for the property is obligated in tithe as it was at first, in their father’s lifetime. “But if not”: that they divided and became partners again and then [the animals] gave birth, they are exempt. “They divided and became partners again” is the explanation of the first clause.

messages.text: Gemara

The verse states: “That you shall set apart for the Lord all that opens the womb; every firstborn male that emerges from an animal that shall be yours belongs to the Lord.” This teaches that the obligation of animal tithe applies only to an animal that belongs to you, i.e., to one owner, but not to an animal owned by partners.

verse.he: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כׇל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר ׀ שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: you shall set apart for GOD every first issue of the womb: every male firstling that your cattle drop shall be GOD’s.

notes.he: אשר יהיה לך הזכרים:
notes.en: GEMARA. “Shall be yours, the males”: “that shall be yours, the males.”

notes.he: דמשמע המיוחד לך אתה נותן ולא של שותפות:
notes.en: And not that of a partnership: for it implies, what is yours alone you give, and not what is of a partnership.

messages.text: One might have thought that the obligation of the tithe does not apply to the animal even if brothers acquired the animals through inheritance from the property in the possession of their father’s house. Therefore, the verse states: “Shall be,” to include animals acquired through inheritance in the obligation of animal tithe.

notes.he: מכל מקום:
notes.en: “Shall be”: in any case.

notes.he: יהיה לך ת"ל יהיה לרבות אותן שקנו מתפוסת הבית שחייבין:
notes.en: “All that opens the womb… shall be yours”: the verse states “shall be” to include those who acquired from the possession of the house, that they are obligated.

messages.text: But this verse is not referring to animal tithe; rather, it is written with regard to firstborn animals.

If it is not needed for the matter of firstborn animals, as the mitzva of sanctifying a firstborn animal does apply in a case of partnership, as it is written, in the plural form: “And you shall bring there your burnt offerings, and your offerings, and your tithes, and the offering of your hand, and your vows, and your gift offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock,” apply the verse to the matter of animal tithe, teaching that it does not apply to an animal owned by partners.

verse.he: וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְזִבְחֵיכֶם וְאֵת מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם וְאֵת תְּרוּמַת יֶדְכֶם וְנִדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקַרְכֶם וְצֹאנְכֶם׃
verse.en: and there you are to bring your burnt offerings and other sacrifices, your tithes and contributions, your votive and freewill offerings, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks.

notes.he: לשון רבים משמע לשנים הוא אומר בקרכם:
notes.en: “And the firstborn of your herd”: plural language; it implies that it is speaking to two, “your herd.”

notes.he: כדכתיב ובכורות בקרכם וצאנכם בריש מכילתין פירשתי ל"ל האי קרא דתיפוק ליה מדאיצטריך למעוטי שותפות כותי:
notes.en: For it applies in a partnership: as it is written, “and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.” At the beginning of our tractate I explained why this verse is needed: one could derive it from the fact that a verse was needed to exclude a partnership with a gentile [which implies that a partnership between Jews is included].

messages.text: There are times when they are obligated both in this, the premium, and in that, animal tithe. And there are times when they are exempt both from this and from that. Furthermore, there are times when they are obligated to add the premium and are exempt from animal tithe; and finally, there are times when they are obligated in animal tithe and are exempt from having to add the premium.
messages.quote: they are obligated to add the premium and are exempt from animal tithe

notes.he: בקלבון ובמעשר:
notes.en: In this and in that: in the premium and in tithe.

messages.text: The guiding principle is that partners are exempt from animal tithe but obligated to pay the premium, whereas in the case of individual ownership one is obligated in the animal tithe but exempt from paying the premium. Therefore, the case where they are obligated both in this, the premium, and in that, animal tithe, is when they divided the money they inherited from their father but did not divide the animals they inherited.

notes.he: וחזרו ונשתתפו ולא חלקו בבהמה דגבי קלבון הוו כשאר שותפים וגבי בהמה הוי תפיסת הבית:
notes.en: That they divided the money: and became partners again, but did not divide the animals. With regard to the premium they are like other partners, and with regard to the animals it is the possession of the house.

messages.text: The case where they are exempt both from this and from that is when they divided the animals but did not divide the money.

The case where they are obligated to pay the premium and are exempt from animal tithe is when they divided up both this and that, the money and the animals, from the estate of their deceased father. Afterward they reestablished a partnership and are therefore partners in the normal sense, rather than co-owners of the original inherited estate, and partners are obligated to pay the premium and are exempt from the animal tithe.

Finally, the case where they are obligated in the animal tithe and are exempt from paying the premium involves brothers who have not divided this or that, the money and the animals of their father’s estate, between them at all. It is therefore considered as though their father is still the sole owner of the estate and is contributing the shekel for the pair of them. Since the estate is under individual ownership, the animal tithe must be separated from the livestock.

messages.caption: Rabbi Yirmeya’s four cases: what the brothers divided decides whether they owe the premium, animal tithe, both or neither.

messages.text: Isn’t it obvious? What is the novelty of Rabbi Yirmeya’s statement?
messages.quote: times when they are exempt both from this and from that

notes.he: דהכי איתה וכל הני יכלינן למידק ממתניתין ומאי קמ"ל ר' ירמיה:
notes.en: Obvious: for so it is, and all of these we could infer from the mishna; what does Rabbi Yirmeya teach us?

messages.text: It was necessary for Rabbi Yirmeya to teach the case where they divided the animals but did not divide the money. It might enter your mind to say that since they divided the animals they have thereby revealed their intent to divide the entire estate. Consequently, the estate stands to be divided, and they should be obligated to pay the premium. Therefore, Rabbi Yirmeya teaches us that they are exempt from paying the premium until they have actually divided the money.

notes.he: דקולא הוא דפטורין מזה ומזה איצטריך ליה לאשמועינן סד"א כיון דחלקו בבהמה ניזיל לחומרא ונימא גלו אדעתייהו דלמיפלג בנכסים נמי קיימי וליחייבו בקלבון:
notes.en: They divided the animals and did not divide the money: since this is a leniency, that they are exempt from both, he needed to teach it. It might enter your mind to go stringently and say that they revealed their intent that they stand to divide the property too, and that they should be obligated in the premium.

notes.he: דעיקר טורח בבהמה היא דטיפולה מרובה וצריכא לסייע כל אחד לחברו ואינהו לא חשו לכוליה האי ופלגי בהמה ודאי גלו אדעתיהו דלמפלג כספים קיימי ואע"ג דלא חלקו עדיין כספים כמי שחלקו דמי וליחייבו בקולבון קמ"ל דלא. אלא מה שחלקו חלקו ומה שלא חלקו לא חלקו:
notes.en: It might enter your mind, since they divided the animals: for the main effort is with the animals, whose care is great, and each needs to help the other; and they did not care about all this and divided the animals. They certainly revealed their intent that they stand to divide the money, and even though they have not yet divided the money it is as if they had, and they should be obligated in the premium. It teaches us that it is not so; rather, what they divided they divided, and what they did not divide they did not divide.

messages.text: The Sages taught this halakha only in a case where they divided kids for goats and goats for kids, i.e., when the two brothers inherited both kids and goats, but one took all the goats and the other all the kids. Since each originally inherited both goats and kids, this division is tantamount to one brother trading his goats for the other’s kids. When they again become partners, they are considered like strangers who join together. Consequently, they are exempt from the animal tithe.
messages.quote: If they divided the inheritance between them and then reentered a partnership

notes.he: דהויא שותפות להיפטר ממעשר בהמה כי חזרו ונשתתפו אלא שחלקו בשומא:
notes.en: They taught only: that it is a partnership, exempting them from animal tithe when they became partners again, only where they divided by valuation.

notes.dh: גדיים כנגד תיישים ותיישים כנגד גדיים
notes.he: לפי שוייהן דהתם ליכא למימר זה חלקו המגיע ממיתת אביהם דוודאי בשעת מיתה זכה זה בחצי הגדיים ובחצי התיישים וזה בחצי הגדיים והתיישים הלכך השתא קנין הוא שזה קונה מזה והולדות שישנם בשעת חלוקה פטורין ממעשר בהמה משום לקוח ואותן העתידים לבא פטורין משום שותפות:
notes.en: Kids against goats and goats against kids: according to their value. There one cannot say that this is the share that came to him at his father’s death, for certainly at the time of death this one acquired half of the kids and half of the goats, and that one half of the kids and of the goats. So now it is an acquisition, in which one acquires from the other: the young that exist at the time of division are exempt from animal tithe as purchased, and those born afterward are exempt because of the partnership.

notes.he: דכי חלקו בהמה פטורין ממעשר אלא שחלקו גדיים כנגד תיישים דהני ודאי לקוחות הן ולא חלוקה גמורה:
notes.en: They taught only: that when they divided the animals they are exempt from tithe, only where they divided kids against goats, for these are certainly purchased, and it is not a complete division.

messages.text: But if they divided kids for kids and goats for goats, so that each takes some of both types, in the normal manner, one can say that this, i.e., the group of animals that each brother takes, is considered his share to which he is entitled from the outset, and no transaction between them has occurred. Consequently, when they reestablish the partnership the estate reverts to its original status as a single entity, and they are therefore obligated to separate animal tithe.

notes.dh: אבל חלקו גדיים כנגד גדיים ותיישים כנגד תיישים
notes.he: אמרינן ברירה וזה חלק המגיע לכל אחד ממיתת אביו ועדיין ירושה היא ושם ירושה עליהן וכי חזרו ונשתתפו הדרא לה תפיסת הבית כמרישא ולא שותפות הוא הילכך ולדות שישנן בשעת חלוקה אינן פטורין משום לקוח ולא העתידין לבא פטורין משום שותפות:
notes.en: But if they divided kids against kids and goats against goats: we say there is retroactive clarification [bereira], and this is the share that came to each one at his father’s death. It is still an inheritance and bears the name of inheritance, and when they became partners again the possession of the house returns as at first, and it is not a partnership. Therefore the young that exist at the time of division are not exempt as purchased, nor are those born afterward exempt because of partnership.

notes.he: זה וזה בשוה לאו לקוחות הן אלא חלוקה גמורה ואומרין לכל אחד הוברר הדבר שזה הוא חלקו ודאי המגיעו וחייבין במעשר:
notes.en: But if they divided this and that equally, they are not purchasers but it is a complete division, and we say of each that it has become clear that this is certainly the share that comes to him; and they are obligated in tithe.

messages.text: Even if they divided the estate in the manner of kids for kids and goats for goats, we do not say that this, the group of animals taken by each brother, is considered his share to which he is entitled from the outset. Therefore, if they reestablish a partnership they are considered like partners and are exempt from separating animal tithe.
messages.quote: they divided kids for kids and goats for goats

notes.he: אין ברירה והוי מרישא לקוחות והדר שותפין:
notes.en: Even if they divided, and so on: there is no retroactive clarification; from the outset they are purchasers, and then partners.

messages.text: This matter is also the subject of a dispute between other amora’im.

notes.he: ר' אלעזר ורבי יוחנן בפלוגתא דרב ענן ורב נחמן פליגי:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree along the lines of the dispute of Rav Anan and Rav Naḥman.

messages.text: The Sages taught this halakha only when they divided nine large goats for ten kids, and ten kids for nine large ones. Since the nine large goats are worth the same as ten kids, this division is tantamount to one brother trading his large goats for the other’s kids. When they again become partners they are considered as strangers who join together, and therefore they are exempt from the animal tithe.

notes.he: חלקו תשעה שמנים כנגד עשרה כחושין היינו נמי ענין לקוחות:
notes.en: They divided nine fat ones against ten lean ones: this too is a matter of purchase.

messages.text: But if they divided nine large goats for nine large goats and ten kids for ten kids, so that each takes some of both types, one can say that this, the group of animals taken by each brother, is considered his share to which he is entitled from the outset, and no transaction between them has occurred. Consequently, when they reestablish the partnership the estate reverts to its original status as a single entity, which means they are obligated to separate animal tithe.

Even if they divided the estate in the manner of nine large goats for nine large goats and ten kids for ten kids, one does not say that this, the group of animals taken by each brother, is considered his share to which he is entitled from the outset. Therefore, if they reestablish a partnership they are considered as partners and are exempt from separating animal tithe.
messages.quote: they divided nine large goats for nine large goats and ten kids for ten kids

notes.he: גדולים כנגד עשרה פחותים דהיינו שומא וליכא למימר ברירה:
notes.en: Nine: large ones against ten lesser ones, which is a division by valuation, and one cannot say there is retroactive clarification.

messages.text: Continued on 57a: Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own line of reasoning, since he also rules that brothers who divided an inheritance are considered purchasers from one another.
